ja: だいはちじゅうさんかい

p.src: Now it is told that in those days the sovereign of Liao raised an army and invaded the borders of the Nine Prefectures Beyond the Mountains. His forces entered by four routes, plundering Shandong and Shanxi and pillaging Henan and Hebei. The prefectures and counties everywhere submitted memorials asking the imperial court for aid, but these passed first through the Bureau of Military Affairs before they could reach the emperor. Privy Councillor Tong Guan conferred with Grand Preceptor Cai Jing, Grand Commandant Gao Qiu, and Yang Jian. They suppressed the memorials without reporting them, merely issuing orders to nearby prefectures to hurry the local troops directly to the rescue—an undertaking as futile as filling a well with snow. Everyone knew of the matter; the emperor alone was kept in ignorance. Just then, the four villainous ministers devised a scheme and had Privy Councillor Tong Guan petition the throne, intending to destroy Song Jiang and his companions. Unexpectedly, a high minister stepped out from behind the imperial screen and stopped him with a shout. It was Su Yuanjing, Chief Grand Commandant of the Palace Command. He addressed the throne: “Your Majesty, Song Jiang and these heroes have only just submitted. All one hundred and eight are bound as closely as hands and feet, and love one another like brothers born of the same parents. They will never consent to be scattered and separated; even in death they will not forsake one another. Why, then, seek once more to take all their lives? These heroes possess no ordinary wisdom and courage. If they should rise in revolt within the capital, how could the danger be quelled? At present Liao has mobilized a hundred thousand troops and occupied the counties belonging to the Nine Prefectures Beyond the Mountains. Memorials pleading for rescue have arrived from every quarter. Troops have repeatedly been dispatched to suppress them and give battle, but it has been like pouring hot water over ants. The enemy’s power is immense, while the government troops sent against them have no sound strategy. Time and again they have lost soldiers and generals, yet the truth has been concealed from Your Majesty and never reported. In my humble opinion, this is the very occasion to dispatch Song Jiang and his entire company of able commanders, leading the troops under them straight to the frontier to subdue the Liao invaders. Letting these heroes win merit and placing their talents at the service of the state would be of genuine benefit. I dare not decide the matter myself, but humbly beg Your Majesty’s wise judgment.” When the emperor had heard Grand Commandant Su’s petition, his imperial countenance brightened with delight. He questioned the assembled officials, and all declared the proposal reasonable. The emperor fiercely rebuked Tong Guan of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the other officials: “You are all slanderous flatterers and ruiners of the realm! Jealous of the worthy and envious of the capable, you block the path of good men, embellish falsehoods and counterfeit sincerity, and have utterly wrecked the great affairs of the court! For the present I shall pardon your offenses and dispense with further inquiry.” The emperor personally wrote an edict appointing Song Jiang Chief Vanguard for the Defeat of Liao and Lu Junyi Deputy Vanguard. The other commanders were to receive offices and titles after they had won merit. He then ordered Grand Commandant Su Yuanjing to carry the edict in person to Song Jiang’s field headquarters and proclaim it there. The emperor withdrew from court, and all the officials dispersed.

p.src: Grand Commandant Su received the imperial command, left the court, and went straight to Song Jiang’s encampment to proclaim it before the army. Song Jiang and the others hastily set out an incense table to receive him. After kneeling to hear the edict, they all rejoiced greatly. Song Jiang and his companions bowed in gratitude to Grand Commandant Su and said, “This is precisely what we all have desired: to exert ourselves for the state, establish merit, and become loyal ministers. Now, through Your Excellency’s gracious and forceful recommendation, we have received a kindness equal to that of our own parents. Only the spirit tablet of Heavenly King Chao at Liangshan Marsh has not yet been properly laid to rest. Nor have the aged parents, children, wives, and dependents of our various households been sent back to their native homes. The fortifications have not yet been demolished, and the warships have not been brought away. May we trouble Your Excellency to petition the throne for an imperial command granting us ten days’ grace? We shall return to the mountain, settle these matters, put our equipment, spears, swords, armor, and horses in order, and then devote ourselves wholly to serving the country.” Grand Commandant Su was delighted to hear this and returned to report it to the emperor. An imperial command was immediately issued that a thousand taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, and five thousand bolts of colored silk be taken from the treasury and bestowed upon the commanders. The Grand Commandant was ordered to draw these goods from the treasury and distribute them at the field headquarters. Those who had families were to receive rewards sufficient to support their dependents for life. Those without families were to receive the rewards in person and keep them themselves. Song Jiang obeyed the edict and gave thanks for the imperial favor, then distributed the rewards, which everyone duly received. Grand Commandant Su returned to court. Before leaving, he instructed Song Jiang: “When you return to the mountain, go quickly and come back quickly. Send someone ahead to inform me; there must be no delay!”

p.src: Song Jiang then assembled the company to discuss who should accompany him back to the mountain. Song Jiang returned with the strategists Wu Yong and Gongsun Sheng, together with Lin Chong, Liu Tang, Du Qian, Song Wan, Zhu Gui, Song Qing, the three Ruan brothers, and more than ten thousand cavalrymen, infantrymen, and naval troops. The rest of the main force remained encamped in the capital under Vanguard Lu. Nothing of note occurred on the journey. When Song Jiang, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, and the others reached Liangshan Marsh, they seated themselves in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. Song Jiang promptly issued orders that every household’s family members pack their belongings and prepare to depart. At the same time, he ordered pigs, sheep, and other sacrificial animals slaughtered and incense, candles, paper money, and paper horses prepared as offerings to Heavenly King Chao, after which the spirit tablet was burned. Then the aged and young of every household were sent back to their original prefectures and counties; mounting carts and horses, they all departed. Next, Song Jiang had his own estate servants escort his family, including the venerable Song and all the household dependents, back to Song Family Village in Yuncheng County, there to resume their lives as law-abiding commoners. He then ordered the three Ruan brothers to select the serviceable vessels. All the remaining small boats unfit for use were distributed among the nearby inhabitants. The inhabitants were permitted to dismantle and carry away any buildings and dwellings on the mountain. The walls of the three passes and the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness and other buildings were all demolished. When every matter had been settled, they mustered the troops and horses and hurried back to the capital.

p.src: Nothing of note occurred on the road, and before long they reached the Eastern Capital. Lu Junyi and the others came out to receive them and escorted them to the main camp. They first sent Yan Qing into the city to inform Grand Commandant Su that Song Jiang wished to take leave of the emperor before leading the great army on its march. On receiving the message, Grand Commandant Su entered the palace and reported it to the emperor. The next day, he brought Song Jiang to the Hall of Martial Glory for an audience with the emperor. The emperor was delighted. After bestowing wine, he spoke in his august voice: “Do not shrink from the hardship of the long road or the exertions of campaigning. Conquer the barbarians and defeat Liao for me, then return swiftly with songs of victory. I shall grant you substantial appointments, and confer titles upon your officers according to their merit. You must not grow lax!” Song Jiang knocked his head upon the floor in gratitude, then held his court tablet upright and petitioned: “Your servant was but a low and insignificant clerk who unwittingly violated the law and was exiled to Jiangzhou. In drunken madness I uttered reckless words and was condemned to public execution. My companions joined forces to rescue me, but with nowhere to flee, I hid myself in the marsh and barely prolonged my wretched life. For the crimes I committed, even ten thousand deaths could not absolve me. Now Your Sacred Majesty, in boundless mercy, has shown me compassion, accepted me into service, and pardoned my former crimes. Even if I laid bare my liver and poured out my heart, I could never repay Your Majesty’s grace. Now that I have received the imperial command, how could I dare do anything but exhaust my strength in loyal service until death itself ends my labors?” The emperor was greatly pleased and again bestowed imperial wine. He ordered that Song Jiang be given a set of gold-painted bow and arrows adorned with magpies, a fine horse with a complete saddle and bridle, and a precious saber. Song Jiang bowed his head in thanks for the imperial favor, took leave of the throne, and departed the palace. Carrying the precious saber, saddled horse, and bow and arrows bestowed by the emperor, he returned to camp and ordered all commanders and officers to prepare to march.

p.src: The next morning, Emperor Huizong ordered Grand Commandant Su to transmit an imperial command appointing two officials of the Secretariat-Chancellery to go to Chenqiao Post Station and feast the three armies under Vanguard Song Jiang. Each soldier was to receive one flask of wine and one catty of meat, issued publicly before the assembled troops, with no deductions permitted. On receiving the imperial command, the Secretariat-Chancellery worked through the watches of the night to prepare the wine and meat, then dispatched two officials to distribute them.

p.src: Meanwhile, the Secretariat had sent two quartermaster officials to Chenqiao Station to distribute wine and meat as a reward to the three armies. Who could have expected these officials to be insatiably corrupt? Serving their own interests and committing fraud, they withheld portions of the wine and meat. They were all treacherous flatterers who coveted bribes. From every bottle of imperial wine they withheld half, and from every jin of meat they withheld six liang. The rations had already been distributed throughout the vanguard. When distribution among the rear guard reached a company of black-clad soldiers, all wearing black helmets and dark armor, they proved to be shield bearers under Xiang Chong and Li Gun. One officer among the soldiers took his wine and meat and examined them. Finding only half a bottle of wine and ten liang of meat, he pointed at the quartermaster official and cursed, “Profit-hungry wretches like you have spoiled the imperial court's gracious reward!” The official shouted, “How am I profit-hungry?” The officer said, “The emperor granted each of us one bottle of wine and one jin of meat, yet you withheld part of both. It is not that we are quarreling over food. What is hateful is that you scoundrels are so utterly unscrupulous—you would scrape the gold from the Buddha's own face!” The official cursed, “You brazen bandit, one of that inexhaustible breed fit only for slicing and slaughter! You still have not shed the rebellious nature of Liangshan Marsh!” The officer flew into a rage and flung the wine and meat straight into the official's face. The official shouted, “Seize this vicious rogue!” The officer immediately drew the saber from beside his round shield. Pointing at him, the official cursed loudly, “You filthy brigand! Whom do you dare kill with that drawn blade?” The officer replied, “When I was at Liangshan Marsh, I killed countless men far more formidable than you. What are thieving officials like you worth?” The official shouted, “You dare kill me?” The officer stepped forward and struck swiftly with his saber. It landed squarely on the official's face, chopping him down to the ground. Everyone cried out and fled. The soldier chased after the man, caught him, and hacked him several more times. Plainly, he could not survive. The soldiers crowded around and refused to move on.

p.src: Xiang Chong and Li Gun immediately galloped off to report the matter to Song Jiang. Song Jiang was greatly alarmed when he heard and consulted Wu Yong about what they should do. Scholar Wu said, “The officials of the Secretariat have never liked us, and now that this has happened, it has given them precisely the opportunity they wanted. Our only course is first to behead the officer as a warning, report the matter to the Secretariat, and halt the troops to await punishment. We must quickly have Dai Zong and Yan Qing slip quietly into the capital and tell Grand Commandant Su every detail. Ask him to inform the emperor beforehand of all the circumstances, so that the Secretariat cannot slander and harm us. Only then can we escape trouble.” Once Song Jiang had settled upon this plan, he rode at full speed to Chenqiao Station. The officer stood motionless beside the corpse. Song Jiang had wine and meat brought out from the station to reward the three armies, then ordered everyone to advance. He then summoned the officer into the station and questioned him about the circumstances. The officer replied, “Again and again he called us rebels of Liangshan Marsh and cursed us as an inexhaustible rabble fit only for slicing and slaughter. I lost my temper and killed him. I have waited here expressly for you, General, to pass judgment upon me.” Song Jiang said, “He was an official appointed by the imperial court—even I stood in fear of him. How could you simply kill him? You are bound to implicate every one of us! Only now have we received the imperial command to go and defeat the Liao. Before we have won the smallest measure of merit, we have instead committed such a deed. What are we to do?” The officer knocked his head upon the ground and submitted himself to death. Song Jiang wept and said, “Since I first went up to Liangshan Marsh, I have never lost a single brother, great or small. But today, now that I have entered official service and am subject to its authority, I cannot act freely even for a single step. Though your fierce spirit has not died, you can no longer behave as you did in former days.” The officer said, “I ask only to accept death.” Song Jiang ordered the officer to drink his fill and become thoroughly drunk, then had him hang himself beneath a tree. Afterward, his head was cut off and displayed as a warning. The quartermaster official's body was placed in a properly furnished coffin, after which a formal report was sent to the Secretariat. There is no need to dwell on it.

p.src: Meanwhile, Dai Zong and Yan Qing slipped secretly into the capital and went straight to Grand Commandant Su's residence, where they told him every detail of the true circumstances. That evening, Grand Commandant Su entered the palace and reported the entire affair to the emperor. The next day, the emperor held court in the Hall of Literary Virtue. An official of the Secretariat stepped from the ranks and memorialized: “A soldier under the newly surrendered commander Song Jiang has killed an appointed official sent by the Secretariat to supervise the distribution of wine and meat. We beg Your Majesty to order an investigation and arrest.” The emperor said, “I would have preferred not to entrust this to your Secretariat, but the affair properly belonged to your office. Yet again, you appointed the wrong men and thus provoked this incident. From whole cartloads of reward wine and meat, only a fraction was actually distributed. The soldiers received the reward in name but not in fact, and so it came to this.” The Secretariat officials memorialized again, “Who would dare withhold anything from the imperial wine?” At this the emperor's wrath thundered forth. He shouted, “I have already sent men to investigate secretly and know every detail. Yet you still use glib words and ingratiating looks to prevaricate before me! Of each bottle of wine I bestowed, half was withheld; of each jin of meat, only ten liang remained. Thus a brave man was driven to fury, and blood was spilled on the spot!” The emperor demanded, “Where is the principal offender?” An official of the Secretariat replied, “Song Jiang has already beheaded the offender and displayed his head as a warning to the troops. He has submitted a report to this office and halted his army to await punishment.” The emperor said, “Since he has already executed the guilty soldier, let Song Jiang's offense of lax discipline be recorded for the time being. When he returns after defeating the Liao, the matter shall be settled according to his merits.” The Secretariat officials withdrew in silence. The emperor immediately issued a decree and dispatched an official to urge Song Jiang to set out. The soldier who had committed the killing was to have his severed head displayed at Chenqiao Station as a warning.

u.src: The next day, the emperor held court in the Hall of Literary Virtue. An official of the Secretariat stepped from the ranks and memorialized: “A soldier under the newly surrendered commander Song Jiang has killed an appointed official sent by the Secretariat to supervise the distribution of wine and meat. We beg Your Majesty to order an investigation and arrest.”
The emperor said, “I would have preferred not to entrust this to your Secretariat, but the affair properly belonged to your office.
Yet again, you appointed the wrong men and thus provoked this incident.
From whole cartloads of reward wine and meat, only a fraction was actually distributed. The soldiers received the reward in name but not in fact, and so it came to this.”
The Secretariat officials memorialized again, “Who would dare withhold anything from the imperial wine?”

At this the emperor's wrath thundered forth. He shouted, “I have already sent men to investigate secretly and know every detail. Yet you still use glib words and ingratiating looks to prevaricate before me!
Of each bottle of wine I bestowed, half was withheld; of each jin of meat, only ten liang remained. Thus a brave man was driven to fury, and blood was spilled on the spot!”
The emperor demanded, “Where is the principal offender?”

An official of the Secretariat replied, “Song Jiang has already beheaded the offender and displayed his head as a warning to the troops. He has submitted a report to this office and halted his army to await punishment.”
The emperor said, “Since he has already executed the guilty soldier, let Song Jiang's offense of lax discipline be recorded for the time being.
When he returns after defeating the Liao, the matter shall be settled according to his merits.”
The Secretariat officials withdrew in silence.

The emperor immediately issued a decree and dispatched an official to urge Song Jiang to set out. The soldier who had committed the killing was to have his severed head displayed at Chenqiao Station as a warning.

p.src: Now Song Jiang was at Chenqiao Station with his troops halted as he awaited punishment, when an imperial envoy arrived and ordered Song Jiang and the others to advance against the Liao, while the offending officer's head was to be exposed as a warning. After Song Jiang had given thanks for the imperial grace, he hung the officer's severed head at Chenqiao Station as a warning and buried the body. Song Jiang wept bitterly for a time, then mounted with tears streaming down his face and led the army northward. Each day the army marched sixty li before pitching camp. In every prefecture and county through which they passed, they took not so much as a hair from the people. Nothing else of note occurred along the way.

p.src: The inscription on the Liao officer’s banner clearly read: “Great General of Liao, Aliqi.” Seeing this, Song Jiang told his generals, “This Liao warrior must not be taken lightly!” Before he had finished speaking, Xu Ning, the Golden Lancer, rode out to battle. Holding his hooked sickle-spear crosswise, he spurred his mount and charged straight before the lines. When the Liao general Aliqi saw him, he cursed loudly: “The Song dynasty is doomed indeed! It appoints brigands as generals, and you dare invade our mighty realm without yet knowing that death is upon you!” Xu Ning shouted, “Wretched general who disgraces his country, how dare you spew such filth!” Both armies raised a thunderous shout. Xu Ning and Aliqi dashed to the center of the field and fought. Their two horses met, and both weapons rose together. Before the two generals had fought much more than thirty bouts, Xu Ning could no longer withstand the Liao warrior and fled toward his own lines. Hua Rong hurriedly took bow and arrow in hand. Just as the Liao general came in pursuit, Zhang Qing had already steadied himself in the saddle and reached into his brocade pouch for a stone. Waiting until the enemy had drawn close enough, he hurled it straight at his face. It struck Aliqi squarely in the left eye, and he somersaulted from his horse. At once Hua Rong, Lin Chong, Qin Ming, and Suo Chao charged out together. They first seized the fine horse, then captured Aliqi alive and carried him back to their lines. When the deputy general Chu Mingyu saw Aliqi brought down, he rushed forward to rescue him, but Song Jiang’s main force closed in from front and rear. Abandoning Miyun County, Chu Mingyu suffered a crushing defeat and fled toward Tanzhou. Song Jiang did not pursue him, but encamped in Miyun County. When they examined the Liao general Aliqi, they found that the stone had smashed his brow and destroyed one eye. Overcome by the agony, he died. Song Jiang ordered that the Liao officer’s remains be cremated. In the register of merit, Zhang Qing was recorded as having won the foremost distinction. Aliqi’s linked tempered-iron armor, gleaming white pear-blossom spear, jeweled lion belt, silver dappled horse, boots, robe, bow, and arrows were all bestowed upon Zhang Qing. That day, still in Miyun County, everyone offered congratulations, and a banquet was laid with wine; there is no need to relate the details.

p.src: The two Liao generals were brothers, dressed alike and wielding the same kind of spear. The Song troops met them and drew up their formation. Dong Ping, the Double-Speared General, rode out and shouted sternly, “Where do you northern brigands come from?” Yelü Guozhen flew into a rage and thundered, “You bandits from a watery lair dare invade our great realm, yet you ask where we come from!” Dong Ping asked no more. Spurring his horse and leveling his spears, he charged straight at Yelü Guozhen. The young Liao general was fierce and unyielding. Far from giving an inch, he raised his steel spear and met the charge head-on. The two horses met, and three spears flew in confusion. Amid the haze of battle dust and the press of murderous fury, the wielder of two spears displayed his singular art, while the wielder of one employed all his marvelous skill. They fought for fifty bouts without either gaining the advantage. Seeing that his elder brother had fought so long, Yelü Guobao feared his strength might fail and ordered the gong sounded from the center ranks. Yelü Guozhen was fighting at fever pitch. Hearing the gong, he urgently tried to disengage, but Dong Ping’s two spears entangled him and would not let him escape. Yelü Guozhen grew flustered, and his spearwork slowed. Dong Ping forced aside the green-shafted spear with his right-hand weapon, then drove the spear in his left straight into the base of the Liao general’s neck. Alas for Yelü Guozhen! His golden crown toppled, his feet flew upward, and he fell from his horse. When his younger brother Yelü Guobao saw him fall, he charged from the formation, riding a single horse and brandishing a spear, to rescue him. In the Song formation, Zhang Qing the Featherless Arrow saw him approach and would not let the chance pass. On horseback he steadied his pear-blossom spear, reached into his brocade pouch, drew out a stone, slapped his mount, and flew before the ranks. Yelü Guobao came flying toward him, and Zhang Qing rushed head-on to meet him. When the two riders were scarcely a dozen yards apart, the Liao general, unsuspecting, thought Zhang Qing meant to engage him in combat. Suddenly Zhang Qing raised his hand and shouted, “Take that!” The stone struck Yelü Guobao squarely in the face, and he somersaulted from his horse. Guan Sheng and Lin Chong drove their troops forward in a sweeping attack. Leaderless, the Liao troops fled wildly in every direction. In a single onslaught they scattered more than ten thousand Liao troops. They gathered up the two Liao officers’ complete saddles and mounts, their two golden tallies, jeweled crowns, robes, and armor, cut off both their heads, and captured over a thousand warhorses. All these were taken to Miyun County and presented to Song Jiang. Song Jiang was delighted. He rewarded the whole army and recorded Dong Ping and Zhang Qing as having earned the second merit. When Tanzhou had been taken, he would report all their deeds together to the throne.

They gathered up the two Liao officers’ complete saddles and mounts, their two golden tallies, jeweled crowns, robes, and armor, cut off both their heads, and captured over a thousand warhorses. All these were taken to Miyun County and presented to Song Jiang.
Song Jiang was delighted. He rewarded the whole army and recorded Dong Ping and Zhang Qing as having earned the second merit.
When Tanzhou had been taken, he would report all their deeds together to the throne.

p.src: Song Jiang conferred with Wu Yong, and that evening wrote out military orders dispatching Lin Chong and Guan Sheng with a body of troops to approach Tanzhou from the northwest. He also ordered Huyan Zhuo and Dong Ping to lead another body of troops and advance from the northeast. Lu Junyi was commanded to lead a force by the southwestern route. “Our central army will take the southeastern road. The instant you hear the cannon, all forces are to advance together.” He then sent the artillerist Ling Zhen together with Li Kui, Fan Rui, Bao Xu, and the shield-bearers Xiang Chong and Li Gun, leading more than a thousand rolling-shield troops, straight beneath the city to fire the signal cannon. The appointed time was the second watch, when land and water forces would advance together. The troops on every route were to respond to one another. Once the commands had been issued, all the forces made their separate preparations to take the city.

p.src: Now Chamberlain Dongxian was holding fast within Tanzhou, anxiously awaiting the arrival of reinforcements. But the remnants of the imperial nephews’ defeated force fled into the city and gave a full account: of the two imperial princes, Yelü Guozhen had been killed by a man wielding twin spears, while Yelü Guobao had been struck from his horse with a stone and captured by a man wearing a blue headscarf. Chamberlain Dongxian stamped his foot and cursed, “That southern savage again! Now that the two imperial nephews are lost, how can I possibly face our sovereign? If we capture that savage in the blue headscarf, I shall have the wretch sliced to pieces!” That evening, Liao soldiers reported to Chamberlain Dongxian, “Five or seven hundred grain boats are moored along both banks of the Lu River, and in the distance more troops are approaching!” Hearing this, Chamberlain Dongxian said, “Those savages know nothing of our waterways and have mistakenly brought their grain boats straight here. The troops on the bank must surely have come in search of them.” He summoned three Liao generals—Chu Mingyu, Cao Mingji, and Yao'er Weikang—and instructed them, “Song Jiang and those savages are bringing up many more troops tonight, while a great number of their grain boats lie in our river. Have Yao'er Weikang lead a thousand troops out of the city in a sudden charge. Chu Mingyu and Cao Mingji are to open the water gate and send boats out with the swift current. If you seize two parts out of every three of their grain fleet, you will have rendered great service!” How the enterprise fared is unknown; a poem bears witness:

p.src: Wondrous schemes have ever differed beyond compare; beneath Tanzhou’s walls the warships stand arrayed. The chamberlain failed to grasp the strategist’s design, and opened the gate himself to clear the way.

p.src: To return to Song Jiang’s forces: at dusk that evening, Li Kui and Fan Rui took the lead on the left flank and brought the infantry beneath the city walls, where they hurled abuse at the enemy. Vice Minister Dongxian ordered Yao’er Weikang to hasten the troops and charge out of the city. The city gates opened, the drawbridge was lowered, and the Liao troops came pouring out. But Li Kui, Fan Rui, Bao Xu, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun, those five valiant men, led a thousand infantrymen—all fierce and brave swordsmen with shields—and held firm beside the drawbridge. How could the enemy troops and horses possibly get out of the city? Meanwhile, Ling Zhen had erected the cannon frames within the army and made ready to fire, waiting only for the appointed moment. They let the defenders shoot arrows from the walls, for shield-bearers guarded them on either side, while Bao Xu raised battle cries from the rear. Though they numbered only a little over a thousand, they had the bearing of more than ten thousand. When Vice Minister Dongxian saw from within the city that his troops could not break through, he urgently ordered Chu Mingyu and Cao Mingji to open the water gate and seize the boats. By then, the commanders of Song Jiang’s naval forces had already lain hidden in their boats, fully prepared and making no move. They saw the water gate open and the sluice boards raised one after another as the warships were let out. When Ling Zhen received word, he first touched off a wind-and-fire cannon. At the roar of the cannon, warships surged forward from both sides to engage the enemy vessels. From the left came Li Jun, Zhang Heng, and Zhang Shun; from the right came the three Ruan brothers. All drove their warships straight into the enemy fleet. When the enemy generals Chu Mingyu and Cao Mingji saw the warships bearing down so fiercely, they could not withstand them. Realizing that troops lay in ambush, they hurried to turn their boats back, but the sailors and soldiers on Song Jiang’s side had already leapt aboard, leaving them no choice but to flee ashore. The six commanders of Song Jiang’s naval forces seized the water gate first. Of the enemy officers guarding the gate, some were slain and the rest fled. Chu Mingyu and Cao Mingji each fled for his life. A fire prepared in advance blazed up over the water gate, and Ling Zhen fired another carriage-box cannon. The projectile flew high into the sky and exploded with a thunderous report. Hearing the ceaseless thunder of cannon fire, Vice Minister Dongxian was frightened out of his wits. Li Kui, Fan Rui, and Bao Xu led the shield-bearers, including Xiang Chong and Li Gun, in a direct assault into the city. Within the city, Vice Minister Dongxian and Yao’er Weikang saw that all the gates had been seized and that Song troops were attacking from all four directions. They had no choice but to mount their horses, abandon the city, and flee through the north gate. Before they had gone two li, they ran straight into Guan Sheng, the Great Blade, and Lin Chong, the Panther Head, who barred their way. The close-woven net of Heaven leaves no room to step; the far-flung snare of Earth allows no escape. How Vice Minister Dongxian ultimately escaped with his life will be revealed in the next chapter.
